definition_en: a party or ceremony held to mark a special occasion, or the act of praising someone publicly
core_image: 人群聚在一处，为一件喜事举杯欢呼
scene: 小镇广场挂满彩灯。The whole village joined the celebration in the square.
sceneCN: 这里 celebration 指「庆祝活动」（第 1 个义项：为纪念喜事而举行的聚会）；句意是全村人都参加了广场上的庆祝活动。

senses.title: A party for a special occasion
senses.definition: a social event held to mark a happy occasion such as a birthday or a victory
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念生日、胜利等喜事而举行的社交活动
senses.example: The team held a celebration after the final match.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛之后球队举行了庆祝活动。
senses.why: The Latin base meant a crowded gathering, and a party is that crowd in its most familiar form.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词基意为人群聚集，而聚会正是这种人群最熟悉的形态。

senses.title: Public praise of someone
senses.definition: the act of praising a person or achievement openly in speech, writing or art
senses.definitionCN: 在言语、文字或艺术中公开赞扬某人或某项成就
senses.example: The film is a celebration of village life.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片是对乡村生活的赞颂。
senses.why: A crowd that gathers to rejoice can also gather to praise, so the festive noun carries the honouring sense.
senses.whyCN: 为欢庆而聚集的人群也能为赞美而聚集，于是这个节庆名词也带上致敬义。

intro.en: Celebration is the noun of celebrate, built on a Latin word for a crowded gathering.
intro.cn: celebration 是 celebrate 的名词形式，词基是拉丁语中表示人群聚集的词。

items.en: Celeber meant crowded, busy or famous.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celeber 意为拥挤、繁忙或著名的。

items.en: Celebratio named a public gathering held to honour someone.
items.cn: celebratio 指为向某人致敬而举行的公众集会。

items.en: Celebration passed through French with the sense of solemn observance.
items.cn: celebration 经法语传来，带有庄严遵行的意味。

items.en: English celebration first names a religious observance and then any festive marking.
items.cn: 英语 celebration 先指宗教仪式，后指任何节庆纪念。

items.en: The word now covers birthdays, national holidays and praise expressed in art.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖生日、国庆以及艺术中的赞颂。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the -celebr- stem, while the meaning group lists other festive gatherings.
note.cn: 形近组保留 -celebr- 词干，近义组列出其他节庆聚会。

entries.definition: to mark a happy occasion
expressing joy at an event
a famous person
a day or period of public rejoicing
entries.definitionCN: 公众欢庆的日子或时期

entries.definition: a social gathering for pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 为消遣而举行的社交聚会

entries.definition: a formal series of acts on a special occasion

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the crowded root, the -tion noun ending and the fixed phrase in celebration of.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拥挤词根、-tion 名词词尾以及固定搭配 in celebration of。

normal.en: Celebration is celebrate plus -ion, the event rather than the act.
normal.cn: celebration 就是 celebrate 加 -ion，指活动而非动作。

normal.en: The root celeber meant crowded, so a good celebration fills the room.
normal.cn: 词根 celeber 意为拥挤，所以好的庆典总把屋子填满。

normal.en: In celebration of is the phrase that links the noun to the reason for the party.
normal.cn: in celebration of 这个搭配把庆典与举办的理由连起来。

normal.en: A celebration of life praises a person rather than merely marking a date.
normal.cn: a celebration of life 是在赞颂一个人，而不只是记一个日子。

normal.en: The plural celebrations only adds an s, with the stress staying on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 复数 celebrations 只加 s，重音仍在第二个音节。

abstract.en: Picture lanterns strung across a square full of talking people.
abstract.cn: 想象彩灯横跨广场，下面全是交谈的人。

abstract.en: Picture a table crowded with dishes and raised glasses.
abstract.cn: 想象一张摆满菜肴、举着酒杯的桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a choir singing in praise of an old teacher.
abstract.cn: 想象合唱团为一位老教师歌唱致敬。

examples.en: The wedding celebration lasted until midnight.
examples.cn: 婚礼庆祝活动一直持续到半夜。

examples.en: There were celebrations in the streets after the result.
examples.cn: 结果公布后街上到处是庆祝活动。

examples.en: The exhibition is a celebration of local craft.
examples.cn: 这场展览是对本地手工艺的赞颂。

dict_mnemonic.text: celebration 里有 celebrate：把「庆祝」这个动作变成一场活动，就成了庆典。

root: 源自拉丁语 celebratio（公众集会致敬），出自 celebrare，词基 celeber 意为拥挤、著名；与 celebrate 同根。

sensesIntro.en: A crowded gathering gives the party sense, and the same crowd turned toward praise gives the honouring sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 人群聚集给出聚会义，同一人群转向赞美则给出致敬义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd gathered around one happy event.
core.cn: 核心意象：围着一件喜事聚集的人群。

branches.en: A birthday or victory party keeps the festive sense.
branches.cn: 生日或胜利聚会保留节庆义。

branches.en: Praise in art turns the gathering into an act of honour.
branches.cn: 艺术中的赞美把聚会变成致敬行为。

branches.en: In celebration of fixes the link between party and reason.
branches.cn: in celebration of 固定了聚会与理由之间的联系。

branches.en: Both put a person or event at the centre of attention.
branches.cn: 两者都把人物或事件放在关注中心。

branches.en: The praise sense often appears in reviews and dedications.
branches.cn: 赞颂义常见于评论与献词中。

intro.en: Celebration keeps the -celebr- stem across verb, noun and adjective.
intro.cn: celebration 在动词、名词与形容词之间保留 -celebr- 词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin celebratio and celebrare are the direct ancestors of the English noun and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 celebratio 与 celebrare 是英语名词和动词的直接祖先。

items.exampleCN: 庆祝活动持续了好几天。
名气没给他带来多少安宁。

items.example: Celebrare is the verb behind it.

latinEntries.example: Celebratio passed into French and English.

definition_en: the smallest living unit of an animal or plant, a small room such as a prison room, or a device that stores electric power
core_image: 一个四面封闭的小格子
scene: 显微镜下能看到微小的结构。Each cell in the sample had a dark centre.
sceneCN: 这里 cell 指「细胞」（第 1 个义项：生物体最小的生命单位）；句意是样本里的每个细胞都有一个深色的中心。

senses.title: The basic unit of life
senses.definition: the smallest part of a living thing that can carry out the processes of life
senses.definitionCN: 生物体中能进行生命活动的最小单位
senses.example: A red blood cell carries oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 红细胞负责运送氧气。
senses.why: Early microscopists saw tiny walled compartments and borrowed the word for a small room.
senses.whyCN: 早期显微镜学家看到一个个有壁的小隔间，就借用了表示小房间的词。

senses.title: A small closed room
senses.definition: a small room, especially one in a prison or a monastery
senses.definitionCN: 小型房间，尤指监狱或修道院中的
senses.example: The prisoner paced his narrow cell.
senses.exampleCN: 犯人在狭窄的牢房里来回踱步。
senses.why: This is the original sense: a small enclosed room, from Latin cella.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义：拉丁语 cella 所指的小型封闭房间。

senses.title: A unit that stores electric power
senses.definition: a container of chemicals that produces electricity, or one unit of a larger battery
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学物质产生电的容器，或电池组中的一节
senses.example: The torch needs a new cell.
senses.exampleCN: 手电筒需要换一节电池。
senses.why: Each battery unit is a sealed compartment, so the room word fits the small power box.
senses.whyCN: 每个电池单元都是密封的小格，于是房间用词正好套在这只电源小盒上。

intro.en: Cell comes from Latin cella, a small room, and every later sense keeps the idea of a closed compartment.
intro.cn: cell 来自拉丁语 cella（小房间），后面每个义项都保留封闭小格的意思。

items.en: Cella meant a small room, a storeroom or a shrine chamber.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cella 指小房间、储藏室或神庙内室。

items.en: Celle named a small room, especially a monk's chamber.
items.cn: 古法语 celle 指小房间，尤指修士的居室。

items.en: Cell covers small rooms in monasteries and prisons.
items.cn: 中古英语 cell 涵盖修道院和监狱的小室。

items.en: Microscopy applies the word to the tiny compartments seen in living tissue.
items.cn: 十七世纪显微镜学把该词用到活体组织中的微小隔间上。

items.en: Electricity adds the battery sense, and compounds such as cell phone spread the word further.
items.cn: 电学又添上电池义，cell phone 等复合词进一步推广该词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the room root through its derivatives, while the meaning group lists other enclosed spaces.
note.cn: 形近组沿房间词根经派生词展开，近义组列出其他封闭空间。

entries.definition: made of cells, or relating to mobile phones
entries.definitionCN: 由细胞组成的，或与移动电话有关的

entries.definition: a person who shares a prison cell
the substance forming plant cell walls
entries.definitionCN: 构成植物细胞壁的物质

entries.definition: a part of a building enclosed by walls
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物中被墙围起的一部分

entries.definition: a large room used for a special purpose
entries.definitionCN: 用于特定用途的大房间

entries.definition: one of several separate sections
entries.definitionCN: 若干分隔部分中的一格

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the little-room root, the blood and prison phrases and the -ular ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用小房间词根、血液与监狱搭配以及 -ular 词尾。

normal.en: Cell is simply Latin cella, a small room, and every sense is still a little box.
normal.cn: cell 就是拉丁语 cella（小房间），每个义项都还是一个小盒子。

normal.en: A prison cell and a biological cell share one shape: a wall around a small space.
normal.cn: 牢房与生物细胞共享一个形状：围住小空间的墙。

normal.en: Cellular means made of cells, and also names the mobile phone network built from small areas.
normal.cn: cellular 意为由细胞组成，也指由小区域构成的移动电话网。

normal.en: Cellmate is cell plus mate, the person sharing that small room.
normal.cn: cellmate 是 cell 加 mate，同住那间小室的人。

normal.en: The plural cells is regular, and the word stays one syllable throughout.
normal.cn: 复数 cells 变化规则，整词始终只有一个音节。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny walled box seen through a microscope lens.
abstract.cn: 想象透过显微镜镜片看到的一个微小带壁盒子。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow stone room with one high window.
abstract.cn: 想象一间窄小的石屋，只有一扇高窗。

abstract.en: Picture a small metal cylinder sliding into a torch.
abstract.cn: 想象一节小金属筒滑进手电筒。

examples.en: The disease attacks healthy cells in the blood.
examples.cn: 这种病攻击血液中的健康细胞。

examples.en: He spent three nights in a police cell.
examples.cn: 他在警局牢房里待了三晚。

examples.en: This lamp runs on a single cell.
examples.cn: 这盏灯只用一节电池。

dict_mnemonic.text: cell 读音短促，像把小盒子「塞」进口袋：细胞、牢房、电池都是一个个封闭的小格。

root: 源自拉丁语 cella（小房间、储藏室），经古法语 celle 进入英语，由房间义扩展到生物细胞与电池单元。

sensesIntro.en: A small room gives the prison sense, the microscope borrows the shape for life, and electricity borrows it again for power units.
sensesIntro.cn: 小房间给出牢房义，显微镜借这个形状指生命单位，电学又借它指电源单元。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small space shut in by walls.
core.cn: 核心意象：四面被墙围住的小空间。

branches.en: Monastery and prison rooms keep the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 修道院与监狱的房间保留最古老的义项。

branches.en: Microscopy transfers the walled box to living tissue.
branches.cn: 显微镜学把带壁盒子转移到活体组织上。

branches.en: Electricity seals chemicals inside a small cylinder.
branches.cn: 电学把化学物质封在小圆筒里。

branches.en: Both are tiny enclosed units separated from neighbours.
branches.cn: 两者都是与邻居隔开的小封闭单元。

branches.en: Both senses keep the physical container visible.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了可见的实体容器。

intro.en: Cell builds adjectives and nouns with -ular, -ulose and the compound mate.
intro.cn: cell 用 -ular、-ulose 以及复合成分 mate 构成形容词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cella also gives cellar and the first element of cemetery.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cella 也给出 cellar，以及 cemetery 的前半部分。

items.meaning: a small room or living unit

items.example: His cellmate taught him to read.
Her cell phone rang in the meeting.
The prison cell had no window.
Cella is the source of cell.
items.exampleCN: cella 是 cell 的来源。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cella 也是 cellar 的来源。

definition_en: a grey powder that hardens when mixed with water and is used in building, or to join things firmly together
core_image: 灰色粉末遇水变硬，把两块石头粘成一体
scene: 建筑工地上尘土飞扬。Workers poured cement into the wooden frame.
sceneCN: 这里 cement 指「水泥」（第 1 个义项：遇水变硬的灰色建筑材料）；句意是工人把水泥倒进木模板里。

senses.title: A powder used in building
senses.definition: a grey powder made from lime and clay that hardens when mixed with water and sand
senses.definitionCN: 由石灰与黏土制成的灰色粉末，与水沙混合后变硬
senses.example: The wall is held together by cement.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙靠水泥黏合在一起。
senses.why: The Latin source meant rough broken stone, and the powder that binds such stones is the modern heir.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是粗糙的碎石，而把碎石黏住的粉末正是它的现代继承者。

senses.title: Something that binds people together
senses.definition: a shared feeling or interest that holds a group together
senses.definitionCN: 把一群人维系在一起的共同情感或利益
senses.example: Common work was the cement of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 共同的工作是这支队伍的黏合剂。
senses.why: If cement holds stones, any force that holds people together can borrow the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然水泥能把石头黏住，任何把人维系在一起的力量都能借用这个词。

senses.title: To make something firm
senses.definition: to make a relationship, agreement or position stronger and harder to break
senses.definitionCN: 使关系、协议或地位更牢固、更难动摇
senses.example: The trip cemented their friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行巩固了他们的友谊。
senses.why: The verb applies the hardening of cement to any bond that becomes solid.
senses.whyCN: 动词把水泥变硬的过程用到任何变得牢固的纽带上。

intro.en: Cement goes back to a Latin word for rough cut stone, and only later named the powder that binds stones.
intro.cn: cement 可追到拉丁语中表示粗糙碎石块词，后来才指把石块黏住的粉末。

items.en: Caementum meant rough stone or rubble used in building.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caementum 指建筑用的粗石或碎石。

items.en: The noun comes from caedere, to cut, because the stone was cut into pieces.
items.cn: 该名词源自动词 caedere（切），因为石料是被切碎的。

items.en: Ciment named the binding material used with rubble in medieval walls.
items.cn: 古法语 ciment 指中世纪砌墙时与碎石同用的黏合材料。

items.en: English cement first means the mortar or binding powder itself.
items.cn: 英语 cement 最初就指灰浆或黏合粉本身。

items.en: Modern chemistry standardises the powder, and the verb extends to firm friendships and agreements.
items.cn: 现代化学使这种粉末标准化，动词义则扩展到牢固的友谊与协议。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the binding family, while the meaning group lists other building and joining materials.
note.cn: 形近组沿黏结词族展开，近义组列出其他建筑与黏合材料。

entries.definition: the process of binding particles together
entries.definitionCN: 把颗粒黏结在一起的过程

entries.definition: having the properties of cement
a machine that mixes cement with sand and water
entries.definitionCN: 把水泥与沙水混合的机器

entries.definition: a hard building material made of cement, sand and gravel
entries.definitionCN: 由水泥、沙和砾石制成的坚硬建材

entries.definition: a soft mixture used to join bricks
entries.definitionCN: 用来砌砖的软质混合物

entries.definition: a substance that sticks things together
entries.definitionCN: 把东西粘在一起的物质

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cut-stone root, the building compounds and the friendship phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用切石词根、建筑复合词以及友谊搭配。

normal.en: Cement comes from a Latin word for cut stone, because it began as rubble in a wall.
normal.cn: cement 来自拉丁语中表示切碎石料的词，因为它最初就是墙里的碎石。

normal.en: Cement, concrete and mortar are a stair: powder, then the mix, then the soft paste between bricks.
normal.cn: cement、concrete、mortar 像三级台阶：粉末、混合料、砖缝里的软浆。

normal.en: To cement a friendship is to let time harden the bond like setting cement.
normal.cn: cement a friendship 就是让时间像凝固的水泥一样把情谊变硬。

normal.en: Cement mixer keeps the word next to the machine that turns the powder into paste.
normal.cn: cement mixer 把词与那台把粉末变成浆的机器放在一起。

normal.en: The noun has no plural in ordinary use, so uncountable is the honest label.
normal.cn: 这个名词日常没有复数，所以标为不可数最诚实。

abstract.en: Picture grey powder sliding from a paper sack.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色粉末从纸袋里滑出来。

abstract.en: Picture a trowel smoothing wet grey paste over bricks.
abstract.cn: 想象泥刀把湿灰浆抹平在砖面上。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pressed together and held by something unseen.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手紧紧相握，被某种看不见的东西固定。

examples.en: The workers mixed cement and sand in a tub.
examples.cn: 工人把水泥和沙在盆里拌匀。

examples.en: A shared language cements the group.
examples.cn: 共同的语言把这个群体凝聚起来。

examples.en: The post is set in cement.
examples.cn: 这根柱子用水泥固定住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: cement 读音近似「塞门特」：把缝隙「塞」满，再「门」一关就黏牢了。

root: 源自拉丁语 caementum（粗石、碎石），出自 caedere（切），经古法语 ciment 进入英语，由石料转指黏合粉末。

sensesIntro.en: Cut stone becomes binding powder, the powder becomes a metaphor for human bonds, and the verb makes any bond harden.
sensesIntro.cn: 切碎的石料变成黏合粉末，粉末变成人际纽带的比喻，动词则让任何纽带变硬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grey powder that hardens and locks two stones together.
core.cn: 核心意象：遇水变硬、把两块石头锁在一起的灰色粉末。

branches.en: The building powder keeps the physical sense closest to the Latin stone.
branches.cn: 建筑粉末义最接近拉丁语的石料本义。

branches.en: A shared interest binds people as cement binds stones.
branches.cn: 共同利益像水泥黏石头一样把人黏在一起。

branches.en: The verb hardens relationships the way cement hardens in air.
branches.cn: 动词让关系变硬，正如水泥在空气中凝固。

branches.en: Both depend on a material that sets and then cannot be moved.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖一种凝固后无法移动的材料。

branches.en: Both apply the builder's craft to human ties.
branches.cn: 两者都把建筑手艺用到人际纽带上。

intro.en: Cement forms abstract nouns with -ation and adjectives with -itious, plus the mixer compound.
intro.cn: cement 用 -ation 构成抽象名词、用 -itious 构成形容词，另有 mixer 复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin caementum and caedere are the stone and cut roots behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caementum 与 caedere 分别是这个词背后的石料与切割词根。

items.example: Cement sets hard in a day.

items.meaning: he or she strengthens a bond

items.exampleCN: 这种土有类似水泥的性质。

items.example: The cement mixer roared all morning.
Caementum named rubble in Roman walls.
items.exampleCN: caementum 指罗马墙中的碎石。

latinEntries.example: Caementum is the source of cement.
latinEntries.exampleCN: caementum 是 cement 的来源。
caedere 解释了切石的画面。

definition_en: a small unit of money worth one hundredth of a dollar or other basic unit, or the hundredth part in expressions such as per cent
core_image: 整块货币被切成一百份后的一份
scene: 他掏出口袋里的零钱。The candy cost fifty cents at the corner shop.
sceneCN: 这里 cent 指「分」（第 1 个义项：主币的百分之一）；句意是街角小店的水果糖卖五十美分。

senses.title: One hundredth of a dollar
senses.definition: a coin or unit of money worth one hundredth of the basic currency unit
senses.definitionCN: 价值为主币百分之一的硬币或货币单位
senses.example: The gum costs twenty cents.
senses.exampleCN: 口香糖二十美分。
senses.why: The Latin word for hundred became the name of the hundredth part of a dollar.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示一百的词，成了美元百分之一的名称。

senses.title: The hundredth part
senses.definition: the element meaning hundred in phrases such as per cent and in old fractions
senses.definitionCN: 在 per cent 等短语及旧式分数中表示一百的成分
senses.example: Prices rose by three per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 价格上涨了百分之三。
senses.why: Before it named a coin, cent simply meant hundred, and that meaning survives in per cent.
senses.whyCN: 在指硬币之前，cent 本义就是一百，这个含义保存在 per cent 里。

intro.en: Cent comes from the Latin word for hundred, which also gave century and percent.
intro.cn: cent 来自拉丁语中表示一百的词，century 与 percent 也出自这里。

items.en: Centum meant one hundred and was pronounced with a hard k.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centum 意为一百，读音开头是硬音 k。

items.en: Cent kept the hundred sense and the spelling that English later borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语 cent 保留一百义以及英语后来借用的拼写。

items.en: English cent first appears in the phrase per cent, meaning by the hundred.
items.cn: 英语 cent 最初见于 per cent，意为按百计算。

items.en: American currency adopts cent for the hundredth part of a dollar.
items.cn: 十八世纪美国货币采用 cent 表示美元的百分之一。

items.en: Cent now names small coins in many countries and survives in percent and century.
items.cn: 如今 cent 指许多国家的小额硬币，并保存在 percent 与 century 中。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the hundred root, while the meaning group lists small coins.
note.cn: 形近组沿「一百」词根展开，近义组列出小额硬币。

entries.definition: a period of one hundred years
a rate in each hundred
relating to a hundredth anniversary
a small coin of low value
a piece of metal money
a five-cent coin in the United States

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie cent to hundred, to century and percent, and to the small coin.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 cent 与一百、century 与 percent，以及小硬币连起来。

normal.en: Cent means hundred, so a cent is one hundredth of a dollar.
normal.cn: cent 意为一百，所以一分就是美元的一百分之一。

normal.en: Century is a hundred years, and percent is per hundred, both hiding the same root.
normal.cn: century 是一百年，percent 是每一百，都藏着同一个词根。

normal.en: Not a cent means no money at all, the smallest possible amount.
normal.cn: not a cent 意为一点钱也没有，是最小的可能金额。

normal.en: The Latin centum began with a k sound, which is why century sounds like sentury.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 centum 开头是 k 音，所以 century 读起来像 sentury。

normal.en: The plural cents is regular and drops no letters.
normal.cn: 复数 cents 变化规则，不省略任何字母。

abstract.en: Picture a single copper coin alone in a palm.
abstract.cn: 想象掌心孤零零一枚铜币。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag ending in ninety-nine cents.
abstract.cn: 想象一个以九十九分结尾的价签。

abstract.en: Picture a pie cut into a hundred thin slices.
abstract.cn: 想象一个派被切成一百薄片。

examples.en: He found a cent under the chair.
examples.cn: 他在椅子底下找到一分钱。

examples.en: The price went up by five per cent.
examples.cn: 价格上涨了百分之五。

examples.en: I do not have a cent on me.
examples.cn: 我身上一分钱也没有。

dict_mnemonic.text: cent 就是「一百」：把一元分成一百份，每份就是一分。

root: 源自拉丁语 centum（一百），经古法语 cent 进入英语；由百义派生出货币单位「分」及 percent、century 等词。

sensesIntro.en: The number hundred gives the hundredth part, and that part becomes a small coin.
sensesIntro.cn: 数字一百给出百分之一，这一份再变成一枚小硬币。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one slice of a whole cut into a hundred parts.
core.cn: 核心意象：整体切成一百份后的一份。

branches.en: The hundredth part survives in per cent and in old fractions.
branches.cn: 百分之一保存在 per cent 与旧式分数中。

branches.en: The coin sense names the hundredth of a dollar.
branches.cn: 硬币义命名美元的百分之一。

branches.en: Not a cent uses the coin to mean the least possible money.
branches.cn: not a cent 用这枚硬币表示最少可能的钱。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the same arithmetic of a hundred.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在同一个「一百」的算术上。

branches.en: Century and percent keep the root visible in other words.
branches.cn: century 与 percent 让这个词根在其他词中保持可见。

intro.en: Cent works as a root in century, percent and centennial rather than taking affixes itself.
intro.cn: cent 更多作为词根出现在 century、percent、centennial 中，本身少接词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin centum, hundred, is the base of a large family across European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centum（一百）是欧洲各语言中一大词族的词基。

items.example: The coin is worth one cent.
The bridge is a century old.
Ten percent of the class was absent.
items.exampleCN: 班上有百分之十的人缺席。

items.example: The old coin was a centime.

latinEntries.example: Centum is the root of cent and century.
latinEntries.exampleCN: centum 是 cent 与 century 的词根。

definition_zh: 中心；中央；中心机构；使集中
definition_en: the middle point of something, a place or building where an activity is based, or to place something in the middle
core_image: 圆规尖脚扎下的那一点，四周等距
scene: 广场四周都是店铺。A fountain stands at the center of the square.
sceneCN: 这里 center 指「中心」（第 1 个义项：广场的中央位置）；句意是广场中央立着一座喷泉。

senses.title: The middle point
senses.definition: the middle point of an area, circle or object, equally distant from the edges
senses.definitionCN: 区域、圆或物体的中点，与边缘等距
senses.example: There is a table in the center of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 房间中央有一张桌子。
senses.why: The Greek source was the fixed point of a compass, and that point is always the middle.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源词是圆规固定不动的那个点，而那个点永远是中央。

senses.title: A place for an activity
senses.definition: a building or area where a particular activity or service is based
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动或服务所在的建筑或区域
senses.example: She works at a health center.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家健康中心工作。
senses.why: A place where people gather for one purpose becomes the centre of that activity.
senses.whyCN: 人们为同一目的聚集的地方，就成了这项活动的中心。

senses.title: To place in the middle
senses.definition: to put something in the middle, or to make one thing the main focus
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放在中间，或使某事物成为主要焦点
senses.example: The discussion centered on pay.
senses.exampleCN: 讨论集中在薪酬问题上。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: to centre is to make something the middle point.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词的反向使用：使集中就是让某物成为中点。

intro.en: Center goes back to a Greek word for a sharp point, the fixed leg of a pair of compasses.
intro.cn: center 可追到希腊语中表示尖点的词，即圆规固定不动的那个脚。

items.en: Kentron meant a sharp point, a goad, and the fixed point of a compass.
items.cn: 希腊语 kentron 指尖点、刺棒，以及圆规的定点。

items.en: Centrum borrowed the Greek word for the middle point of a circle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 借入该希腊词，指圆的中心点。

items.en: Centre carried the geometric sense into medieval French.
items.cn: 古法语 centre 把几何义带入中世纪法语。

items.en: English centre names the middle of a circle and then of any space.
items.cn: 中古英语 centre 先指圆心，后指任何空间的中央。

items.en: American spelling drops the -re, and the word extends to shopping centres and centres of research.
items.cn: 美式拼写去掉 -re，词义扩展到购物中心与研究中心。

note.en: The look-alike group includes the British spelling and the derived forms, while the meaning group lists other middle words.
note.cn: 形近组包含英式拼写与派生形式，近义组列出其他表示中部的词。

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same word
in the middle, or most important
entries.definitionCN: 位于中央的，或最重要的

entries.definition: a person with middle political views
the point equally far from two sides
the central part of something
the central point of activity

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the compass-point root, the -al and -ist endings and the shopping phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用圆规定点词根、-al 与 -ist 词尾以及购物搭配。

normal.en: A centre is the point where the compass needle stands still, the one fixed place.
normal.cn: 中心就是圆规针尖不动的那一点，唯一固定的位置。

normal.en: Central and centrist keep the same root and shift it to an adjective and a person.
normal.cn: central 与 centrist 保留同一词根，分别转为形容词与人。

normal.en: Centre in British spelling and center in American spelling differ by two letters.
normal.cn: 英式 centre 与美式 center 只差两个字母的位置。

normal.en: Center on means to make one subject the fixed point of a discussion.
normal.cn: center on 意为让一个话题成为讨论的定点。

normal.en: Center of attention is the same picture applied to people in a room.
normal.cn: center of attention 把同一画面用到房间里的人身上。

abstract.en: Picture a compass leg pressed into paper while the other draws a circle.
abstract.cn: 想象圆规一只脚扎进纸里，另一只脚画出圆圈。

abstract.en: Picture a fountain in the middle of a crowded square.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤广场正中的一座喷泉。

abstract.en: Picture everyone in a room turning toward one speaker.
abstract.cn: 想象满屋人都转向同一位发言者。

examples.en: The hotel is in the center of town.
examples.cn: 这家旅馆位于镇中心。

examples.en: The new center will help young families.
examples.cn: 这个新中心将帮助年轻家庭。

examples.en: Her research centers on soil quality.
examples.cn: 她的研究集中在土壤质量上。

dict_mnemonic.text: center 里有 cent：把一百样东西摆匀，正中间那一点就是中心。

root: 源自希腊语 kentron（尖点、圆规定点），经拉丁语 centrum 与古法语 centre 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The compass point gives the geometric middle, a gathering place gives the institutional sense, and the verb makes something that middle.
sensesIntro.cn: 圆规定点给出几何中心，聚集之地给出机构义，动词则让某物成为那个中心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the fixed point of a compass, equally distant from every edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：圆规的定点，与每条边都等距。

branches.en: Geometry keeps the exact middle of a circle or room.
branches.cn: 几何义保留圆或房间的精确中点。

branches.en: A building where one activity gathers becomes its centre.
branches.cn: 某项活动聚集的建筑成为它的中心。

branches.en: The verb makes a topic or object the fixed point.
branches.cn: 动词义让话题或物件成为定点。

branches.en: Both senses involve one place that everything else is measured from.
branches.cn: 两个义项都涉及一个用来衡量其他一切的地点。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of concentrating attention in one spot.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享把注意力集中到一处之意。

intro.en: Center forms -al, -ally and -ist derivatives and keeps a British spelling with -re.
intro.cn: center 构成 -al、-ally、-ist 派生词，并有 -re 的英式拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin centrum is the bridge from Greek kentron to the modern English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 是从希腊语 kentron 到现代英语词的桥梁。

items.example: The center is marked in red.
The city has three sports centers.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市有三个体育中心。

items.example: He centered the picture on the wall.

items.meaning: the act of placing in the middle
items.example: Centering the text took a moment.
items.exampleCN: 把文字居中花了一会儿。

items.meaning: in the middle or most important

items.exampleCN: 这套公寓位于中心地段。
中间派候选人赢得了席位。

latinEntries.example: Centrum passed into French as centre.
latinEntries.exampleCN: centrum 传入法语成为 centre。

definition_en: relating to a temperature scale in which water freezes at zero degrees and boils at one hundred degrees
core_image: 把冰点到沸点均匀刻成一百格
scene: 冬天的早晨，窗上结了霜。The thermometer showed five degrees centigrade below zero.
sceneCN: 这里 centigrade 指「摄氏度」（第 1 个义项：以冰点为零度、沸点为一百度的温标）；句意是温度计显示零下五摄氏度。

senses.title: The hundred-step temperature scale
senses.definition: a scale of temperature with zero at the freezing point of water and one hundred at the boiling point
senses.definitionCN: 以水的冰点为零度、沸点为一百度的温标
senses.example: Water boils at one hundred degrees centigrade.
senses.exampleCN: 水在一百摄氏度沸腾。
senses.why: The word says exactly what the scale does: a hundred equal steps from freezing to boiling.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把温标的做法说得很明白：从冰点到沸点均分一百格。

senses.title: Divided into a hundred degrees
senses.definition: describing any scale or instrument marked off in one hundred equal parts
senses.definitionCN: 形容任何被划成一百等份的刻度或仪器
senses.example: The old instrument had a centigrade dial.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧仪器有一个百分度刻度盘。
senses.why: Before it named a particular thermometer, the adjective simply meant hundred-stepped.
senses.whyCN: 在专指某种温度计之前，这个形容词只表示「分成一百格的」。

intro.en: Centigrade is a learned compound of Latin hundred and Latin step, naming a scale of one hundred steps.
intro.cn: centigrade 是拉丁语「一百」与「步、度」的学术复合词，指一百格的温标。

items.en: Centum meant one hundred.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centum 意为一百。

items.en: Gradus meant a step, a degree or a rank.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gradus 意为步、度或等级。

items.en: French centigrade was coined for a scale divided into a hundred degrees.
items.cn: 法语 centigrade 为分成一百度的温标而造。

items.en: English adopts centigrade as the thermometer with a hundred-step scale spreads.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语采用 centigrade，正值百格温标温度计推广。

items.en: Celsius is now the official name, while centigrade survives in everyday speech.
items.cn: 如今官方名称是 Celsius，centigrade 仍活在日常口语中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects other centi- compounds, while the meaning group lists temperature scales.
note.cn: 形近组收其他 centi- 复合词，近义组列出温标名称。

entries.definition: one hundredth of a gram
one hundredth of a metre
a long many-legged crawling animal
entries.definitionCN: 身体细长、多足的爬行动物

entries.definition: the official name of the hundred-step scale
a scale with freezing at thirty-two degrees
entries.definitionCN: 冰点为三十二度的温标

entries.definition: a scale starting at absolute zero
entries.definitionCN: 从绝对零度开始的温标

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into hundred and step and link it to the freezing and boiling points.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把词拆成「一百」和「度」，并把它与冰点、沸点连起来。

normal.en: Centi means hundred and grade means step, so centigrade is a hundred steps between ice and steam.
normal.cn: centi 意为一百，grade 意为度，所以 centigrade 就是冰与蒸汽之间的一百格。

normal.en: Centigrade and centimeter share the centi- prefix, both cutting a unit into a hundred parts.
normal.cn: centigrade 与 centimeter 共享 centi- 前缀，都把单位分成一百份。

normal.en: Degrees centigrade puts the scale after the number, as in five degrees centigrade.
normal.cn: degrees centigrade 把温标放在数字后，如五摄氏度。

normal.en: Celsius is the modern official name, but centigrade still appears in weather reports.
normal.cn: Celsius 是现代正式名称，centigrade 仍出现在天气播报里。

normal.en: The adjective never changes form, so there is nothing to add for plural or comparison.
normal.cn: 这个形容词没有形态变化，复数或比较都无需加词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a glass tube with a mark every hundredth of the way.
abstract.cn: 想象一根玻璃管，每百分之一的路程刻一道线。

abstract.en: Picture ice at the bottom mark and steam at the top mark.
abstract.cn: 想象底部刻度是冰，顶部刻度是蒸汽。

abstract.en: Picture a winter window with frost at minus five.
abstract.cn: 想象零下五度时结霜的冬日窗户。

examples.en: The room was about twenty degrees centigrade.
examples.cn: 房间大约二十摄氏度。

examples.en: Water freezes at zero degrees centigrade.
examples.cn: 水在零摄氏度结冰。

examples.en: The old thermometer is marked in centigrade.
examples.cn: 这支旧温度计按摄氏度刻度。

dict_mnemonic.text: centi 是一百，grade 是度：把冰到沸之间分成一百度，就是 centigrade。

root: 由拉丁语 centum（一百）与 gradus（步、度）复合而成，经法语 centigrade 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The literal hundred steps give the temperature scale, and the same compound describes any dial divided the same way.
sensesIntro.cn: 字面的一百格给出温标义，同一复合词也形容任何如此划分的刻度盘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tube marked off into one hundred equal steps.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根刻成一百等份的管子。

branches.en: The hundred-step scale fixes zero at freezing and a hundred at boiling.
branches.cn: 百格温标把零度定在冰点、一百度定在沸点。

branches.en: Any instrument with a hundred divisions can take the adjective.
branches.cn: 任何分成一百格的仪器都能用这个形容词。

branches.en: Both senses come straight from the two Latin parts of the word.
branches.cn: 两个义项都直接来自这个词的两个拉丁成分。

branches.en: Celsius now carries the official name for the same scale.
branches.cn: Celsius 如今是同一温标的正式名称。

branches.en: The adjective sense is older and more general than the thermometer.
branches.cn: 形容词义比温度计义更古老、更宽泛。

intro.en: Centigrade is built from two Latin roots and shares the centi- prefix with many metric words.
intro.cn: centigrade 由两个拉丁词根构成，并与许多公制词共享 centi- 前缀。

latinIntro.en: Centum, hundred, and gradus, step, are the two elements of the compound.
latinIntro.cn: centum（一百）与 gradus（步、度）是这个复合词的两个成分。

items.example: The dose is a few centigrams.
The crack is two centimeters wide.
A centipede ran under the stone.

items.meaning: the official name of the scale
items.exampleCN: 科学界用 Celsius 取代了 centigrade。

latinEntries.exampleCN: centum 给出 centi- 前缀。
gradus 给出 grade 与 degree。

definition_en: a unit of length equal to one hundredth of a metre
core_image: 一米被平均分成一百小格，每格就是一小段
scene: 她用尺子量纸片的边。The strip was three centimetres wide.
sceneCN: 这里 centimetre 指「厘米」（第 1 个义项：百分之一米的长度单位）；句意是这条纸片有三厘米宽。

senses.title: One hundredth of a metre
senses.definition: a metric unit of length equal to one hundredth of a metre
senses.definitionCN: 等于百分之一米的公制长度单位
senses.example: The book is two centimetres thick.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书有两厘米厚。
senses.why: Centi- means hundredth and metre is the base unit, so the word states the fraction directly.
senses.whyCN: centi- 意为百分之一，metre 是基本单位，词本身就写明了这个分数。

senses.title: A small mark on a ruler
senses.definition: one of the small divisions marked on a measuring rule or tape
senses.definitionCN: 尺子或卷尺上标出的小格之一
senses.example: Count the centimetres from the edge.
senses.exampleCN: 从边缘开始数厘米格。
senses.why: The unit becomes a visible mark once a ruler prints it, so the word also names the division itself.
senses.whyCN: 当尺子把单位印出来，它就成了一处可见的刻度，于是这个词也指那道分格。

intro.en: Centimetre is a French metric coinage joining Latin hundred to the Greek-based word for measure.
intro.cn: centimetre 是法语公制新造词，把拉丁语「一百」与源自希腊语的「量度」拼在一起。

items.en: Metron meant a measure, and it reached Latin as metrum.
items.cn: 希腊语 metron 意为量度，进入拉丁语作 metrum。

items.en: Centum meant one hundred and supplied the centi- prefix.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centum 意为一百，提供 centi- 前缀。

items.en: French scientists coined centimetre during the creation of the metric system.
items.cn: 法国科学家在建立公制时造出 centimetre。

items.en: English adopts the word as metric measures spread across Europe.
items.cn: 随着公制在欧洲推广，英语在十八世纪采用该词。

items.en: American spelling writes centimeter, while British usage keeps centimetre.
items.cn: 美式拼写写作 centimeter，英式保留 centimetre。

note.en: The look-alike group collects centi- and metric compounds, while the meaning group lists nearby length units.
note.cn: 形近组收 centi- 与公制复合词，近义组列出相近的长度单位。

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same unit
one hundredth of a gram
a long crawling animal with many legs
one thousandth of a metre
the basic metric unit of length
a unit of length of about two and a half centimetres
entries.definitionCN: 约合二点五厘米的长度单位

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into hundred and measure, and link it to the ruler.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把词拆成「一百」和「量度」，并与尺子联系起来。

normal.en: Centi is a hundredth and metre is the base, so a centimetre is a hundredth of a metre.
normal.cn: centi 是百分之一，metre 是基本单位，所以一厘米就是一米的百分之一。

normal.en: Centimetre, millimetre and kilometre form a ladder of metric prefixes around the same base.
normal.cn: centimetre、millimetre、kilometre 围绕同一词基构成公制前缀阶梯。

normal.en: British spelling keeps -re and American spelling uses -er, as in centre and center.
normal.cn: 英式保留 -re，美式用 -er，与 centre、center 的差别相同。

normal.en: Square centimetre and cubic centimetre show the unit used for area and volume.
normal.cn: square centimetre 与 cubic centimetre 展示该单位用于面积与体积。

normal.en: Centimetre by centimetre means moving forward in very small steps.
normal.cn: centimetre by centimetre 意为一点一点地向前挪。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler marked with tiny numbered gaps.
abstract.cn: 想象一把标着细密编号小格的尺子。

abstract.en: Picture a fingernail about one small unit wide.
abstract.cn: 想象一片约一个小单位宽的指甲。

abstract.en: Picture a line of paper strips laid end to end.
abstract.cn: 想象一条条纸片首尾相接排开。

examples.en: The plant grew five centimetres in a week.
examples.cn: 这株植物一周长了五厘米。

examples.en: Cut the cloth ten centimetres from the edge.
examples.cn: 从布边量出十厘米再剪。

examples.en: The table is ninety centimetres high.
examples.cn: 这张桌子九十厘米高。

dict_mnemonic.text: centi 是一百，metre 是米：把一米切成一百段，每段就是厘米。

root: 由拉丁语 centum（一百）与希腊—拉丁语 metrum（量度）复合，经法语 centimètre 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One hundredth of a metre gives the unit, and a ruler turns that unit into a visible mark.
sensesIntro.cn: 一米的百分之一给出单位义，尺子又把该单位变成可见的刻度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a metre cut into one hundred equal short pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：一米被切成一百段等长的小段。

branches.en: The unit sense fixes the exact fraction of a metre.
branches.cn: 单位义固定了相对一米的精确分数。

branches.en: The printed division makes the same unit visible on a tool.
branches.cn: 印出的分格让同一单位在工具上可见。

branches.en: Both rest on the centi- fraction and the metre base.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在 centi- 分数与 metre 词基上。

branches.en: Square and cubic compounds extend the unit to area and volume.
branches.cn: 平方与立方复合词把该单位扩展到面积与体积。

branches.en: The metric system keeps this unit standard across most countries.
branches.cn: 公制让这个单位在多数国家通用。

intro.en: Centimetre joins the centi- prefix to metre, and its family includes many metric compounds.
intro.cn: centimetre 把 centi- 前缀接到 metre 上，其词族包含许多公制复合词。

latinIntro.en: Centum, hundred, and metrum, measure, are the two elements of the word.
latinIntro.cn: centum（一百）与 metrum（量度）是这个词的两个成分。

items.example: The wire is one millimetre thick.
Metron is the Greek source of metre.
items.exampleCN: metron 是 metre 的希腊语来源。
centum 给出 centi- 前缀。

items.example: The ruler is marked in centimetres.
items.exampleCN: 这把尺子以厘米为刻度。

definition_zh: 中央的；中心的；主要的；核心的
definition_en: in the middle of an area, or most important and basic to a system or idea
core_image: 从中心向四周辐射的那一点
scene: 老城区的街道都通向同一个广场。The central square is where all the buses stop.
sceneCN: 这里 central 指「中心的」（第 1 个义项：位于城区中央的）；句意是中心广场是所有公交车的停靠处。

senses.title: In the middle of an area
senses.definition: located in the middle of a place, area or system
senses.definitionCN: 位于某地、某区域或某系统的中部
senses.example: The flat is in a central location.
senses.exampleCN: 这套公寓位于中心地段。
senses.why: Central is simply the adjective of centre, so it names whatever sits at the middle point.
senses.whyCN: central 就是 centre 的形容词，因此指位于中点的事物。

senses.title: Most important or basic
senses.definition: of the greatest importance to a system, argument or activity
senses.definitionCN: 对某个体系、论证或活动最重要的
senses.example: Trust is central to any friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 信任对任何友谊都至关重要。
senses.why: What sits at the centre holds the rest together, so the middle position becomes a metaphor for importance.
senses.whyCN: 位于中心的东西把其余部分维系住，于是中央位置成了重要性的比喻。

intro.en: Central is the Latin adjective of centrum, the middle point, and English built it directly on centre.
intro.cn: central 是拉丁语 centrum（中点）的形容词，英语直接在 centre 上加后缀构成。

items.en: Kentron meant a sharp point and the fixed leg of a compass.
items.cn: 希腊语 kentron 指尖点与圆规的固定脚。

items.en: Centrum named the middle point, and centralis meant belonging to it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 指中点，centralis 意为属于中点的。

items.en: Central reached English through French use in geometry and government.
items.cn: central 经法语在几何与行政领域的使用进入英语。

items.en: English central first describes physical positions near the middle.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 central 先描述靠近中部的物理位置。

items.en: The word spreads to central government, central heating and ideas central to an argument.
items.cn: 词义扩展到中央政府、集中供暖以及论证的核心观念。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the centre family, while the meaning group lists other words for importance and middleness.
note.cn: 形近组沿 centre 词族展开，近义组列出表示重要与居中的词。

entries.definition: the middle point
in a central position
to bring under one control
largest or most important
highest in rank or importance
equally far from both sides

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the centre stem, the -ly and -ize family and the government phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 centre 词干、-ly 与 -ize 词族以及政府搭配。

normal.en: Central is centre plus -al, just as national is nation plus -al.
normal.cn: central 就是 centre 加 -al，正如 national 是 nation 加 -al。

normal.en: Central to is the phrase that turns the physical middle into importance.
normal.cn: central to 这个搭配把物理中央转成重要性。

normal.en: Central bank and central government show power gathered at one point.
normal.cn: 中央银行与中央政府展示权力集中到一点。

normal.en: Central heating sends warmth from one central source to every room.
normal.cn: 集中供暖把热从一处中心源送到每个房间。

normal.en: More central and most central use helpers, while centrally is the adverb.
normal.cn: 比较级最高级用 more 与 most，副词形式是 centrally。

abstract.en: Picture spokes running out from one hub to a wheel rim.
abstract.cn: 想象辐条从轮毂伸向轮圈。

abstract.en: Picture a square where every street meets.
abstract.cn: 想象所有街道交汇的广场。

abstract.en: Picture a single boiler warming a whole building.
abstract.cn: 想象一台锅炉温暖整栋楼。

examples.en: The library is in a central part of the city.
examples.cn: 图书馆位于城市中心地带。

examples.en: This question is central to the whole debate.
examples.cn: 这个问题对整个辩论至关重要。

examples.en: The central bank raised interest rates.
examples.cn: 中央银行提高了利率。

dict_mnemonic.text: central 里有 centre：凡是位于 centre 的，就是 central；凡事都围着它转，也就是最重要的。

root: 源自拉丁语 centralis，出自 centrum（中点），与 centre 同根，经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The middle point gives the positional sense, and whatever holds the middle together becomes the important sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 中点给出位置义，而维系中心的事物则变成重要义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one point from which everything else spreads out.
core.cn: 核心意象：其他一切由之向外展开的那一点。

branches.en: Physical position keeps the literal middle.
branches.cn: 物理位置保留字面上的中央。

branches.en: Importance borrows the pull of the middle point.
branches.cn: 重要性借用了中点的吸引力。

branches.en: Central bank and central heating apply the position to institutions and buildings.
branches.cn: 中央银行与集中供暖把位置义用到机构与建筑上。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of one point holding the rest.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「一点维系其余」的意思。

branches.en: Central to appears in arguments about values and causes.
branches.cn: central to 常出现在关于价值与原因的论证中。

intro.en: Central expands with -ly and -ize, and its base centre supplies the noun.
intro.cn: central 用 -ly 与 -ize 扩展，词基 centre 提供名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin centralis and centrum are the adjective and noun behind the English pair.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centralis 与 centrum 是英语这对词的形容词与名词来源。

items.meaning: in the middle or most important
items.meaningCN: 位于中央的或最重要的

latinEntries.example: Centrum is the noun behind it.

definition_zh: 中心；中央；中心场所；把…置于中央
definition_en: the middle point of something, a place where an activity is based, or to move something to the middle
core_image: 一个圆里到四周距离都相等的那一点
scene: 广场正中有一处喷泉，四条街都通向它。The centre of the square holds a fountain.
sceneCN: 这里 centre 指「中心」（第 1 个义项：与四周等距的中点）；句意是广场的中心有一座喷泉。

senses.title: The middle point
senses.definition: the point or part of something that is equally distant from all its sides
senses.definitionCN: 某物到各边距离相等的那一点或那一部分
senses.example: Draw a dot in the centre of the circle.
senses.exampleCN: 在圆心画一个点。
senses.why: The word comes straight from the Latin name for the fixed point of a compass, so the middle point is its oldest and plainest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接来自拉丁语对圆规固定点的称呼，因此中点是最古老也最朴素的义项。

senses.title: A place for an activity
senses.definition: a building or area where a particular activity is carried on
senses.definitionCN: 开展某项活动的建筑或区域
senses.example: She works at a health centre downtown.
senses.exampleCN: 她在市中心的健康中心工作。
senses.why: An activity gathers people at one spot, so the physical middle turns into the place where that activity is concentrated.
senses.whyCN: 一项活动把人聚到一处，于是物理中点变成了该活动集中的地方。

senses.title: To put in the middle
senses.definition: to move something to the middle, or to make something the main focus
senses.definitionCN: 把某物移到中间，或使某物成为主要焦点
senses.example: Centre the picture on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 把画挂在墙的正中。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb once people speak of placing a thing at that middle point.
senses.whyCN: 当人们说到把东西放到那个中点时，名词就转为动词。

intro.en: Centre goes back to the Greek word for a compass point and reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: centre 可追溯到希腊语中圆规尖点的说法，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.en: Kentron named the sharp point and the fixed leg of a drawing compass.
items.cn: 希腊语 kentron 指尖点与圆规固定的那一脚。

items.en: Centrum became the standard word for the middle point of a circle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 成为圆的中心点的标准说法。

items.en: Old French centre carried the word into English writing on geometry.
items.cn: 古法语 centre 把这个词带入英语的几何著作。

items.en: English centre first appears as a term in astronomy and geometry.
items.cn: 英语 centre 最初作为天文学与几何学术语出现。

items.en: The word extends to shopping centres, research centres and the verb to centre.
items.cn: 词义扩展到购物中心、研究中心以及动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group covers the centre family and its American spelling, while the meaning group gives other words for a middle or a hub.
note.cn: 形近组涵盖 centre 词族及其美式拼写，近义组给出表示中部或枢纽的其他词。

entries.definition: the same word spelled the American way
in the middle or most important
a person with middle political views
the part equally far from both ends
the most important part of something
the central point of an activity or network

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the compass point, the shopping phrases and the -al and -ed family.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用圆规尖点、购物场所搭配以及 -al 与 -ed 词族。

normal.en: Imagine a compass standing on one leg: that still point is the centre.
normal.cn: 想象一只脚立住的圆规，那个不动的尖点就是 centre。

normal.en: City centre, shopping centre and research centre all name one busy spot.
normal.cn: city centre、shopping centre 与 research centre 都指一处热闹的地点。

normal.en: Centre on means to make one thing the focus, as a camera centres on a face.
normal.cn: centre on 意为把某物当作焦点，就像相机对准一张脸。

normal.en: British spelling keeps -re, while American spelling turns it into -er.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留 -re，美式则改成 -er。

normal.en: Central is centre plus -al, and centred is centre plus -ed.
normal.cn: central 是 centre 加 -al，centred 是 centre 加 -ed。

abstract.en: Picture rings spreading out from one dot on still water.
abstract.cn: 想象静水上一圈圈从一个点散开的波纹。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel with every spoke meeting at one hub.
abstract.cn: 想象车轮的每根辐条都交于一个轮毂。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd closing in around a street performer.
abstract.cn: 想象人群围拢到街头艺人四周。

examples.en: There is a fountain at the centre of the park.
examples.cn: 公园正中有一座喷泉。

examples.en: The new sports centre opens next month.
examples.cn: 新的体育中心下月开放。

examples.en: The discussion centred on pay and working hours.
examples.cn: 讨论集中在工资与工时上。

dict_mnemonic.text: centre 与 central 同根：抓住中心的那一点，其余部分都围着它转。

root: 源自希腊语 kentron（尖点），经拉丁语 centrum 与古法语 centre 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The geometric middle point comes first, a place of activity grows out of it, and the verb turns the middle into an action.
sensesIntro.cn: 几何中点义最先出现，活动场所义由它生长出来，动词义又把「中间」变成动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one point where all equal distances meet.
core.cn: 核心意象：所有等距线交汇的那一点。

branches.en: Geometry supplies the literal middle point.
branches.cn: 几何义提供字面上的中点。

branches.en: Gathering turns the middle into a place of activity.
branches.cn: 人的聚集把中点变成活动场所。

branches.en: The verb moves an object towards that middle.
branches.cn: 动词义把物体移向那个中间。

branches.en: Both senses keep the pull of one central spot.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留单一中心点的吸引力。

branches.en: A centre of study and to centre on an issue share the same focus.
branches.cn: 研究中心与聚焦某个议题共享同一焦点。

intro.en: Centre yields central, centrally and centred, and the base supports many place names.
intro.cn: centre 派生出 central、centrally 与 centred，词基还支撑大量场所名称。

latinIntro.en: Latin centrum and centralis stand behind the noun and adjective pair.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 与 centralis 是这对名词与形容词的来源。

items.example: The text is centred on the page.

items.meaning: to bring together at one point

latinEntries.exampleCN: centrum 以 centre 的形式进入英语。

definition_zh: 世纪；一百年；（板球）一百分
definition_en: a period of one hundred years, or a score of one hundred in cricket
core_image: 日历上整整一百年排成的一长条
scene: 钟楼每小时敲一次，记录着时间流逝。The tower has stood for a century.
sceneCN: 这里 century 指「世纪」（第 1 个义项：一百年的时间）；句意是这座钟楼已经矗立了一个世纪。

senses.title: A hundred-year period
senses.definition: a period of one hundred years, often counted from a fixed starting point
senses.definitionCN: 一百年的时间，常从某个固定起点算起
senses.example: The bridge was built in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥建于上个世纪。
senses.why: The Latin source named a group of one hundred soldiers, and the same count was later applied to years.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指一百名士兵组成的一队，后来同样的计数被用到年份上。

senses.title: A score of one hundred
senses.definition: a score of one hundred points, especially in cricket
senses.definitionCN: 一百分的得分，尤指板球比赛
senses.example: He scored a century in the final match.
senses.exampleCN: 他在决赛中拿到一百分。
senses.why: The Latin word already counted a block of one hundred men, so sports simply reuse that block for runs.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原词本就把一百人算作一队，运动只是把这一百用到了得分上。

intro.en: Century comes from the Latin word for a unit of one hundred soldiers, and later came to count years.
intro.cn: century 源自拉丁语中一百名士兵的编制单位，后来才用来数年份。

items.en: Centum meant one hundred and stood at the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centum 意为一百，是整族词的根。

items.en: Centuria named a company of a hundred Roman soldiers under a centurion.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centuria 指由百人队长统领的一百名罗马士兵。

items.en: Old French centurye kept the sense of a group of one hundred.
items.cn: 古法语 centurye 保留「一百个一组」的意思。

items.en: English century begins to mean a period of one hundred years.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 century 开始表示一百年的时间。

items.en: The word also names a hundred runs in cricket and a hundred years in history.
items.cn: 这个词还指板球中的一百分与历史学中的一百年。

note.en: The look-alike group collects cent- words from the same Latin hundred, while the meaning group lists other units of time.
note.cn: 形近组收集同出拉丁语「一百」的 cent- 词，近义组列出其他时间单位。

entries.definition: the officer of a hundred Roman soldiers
entries.definitionCN: 统领一百名罗马士兵的军官

entries.definition: happening every hundred years
a coin worth one hundredth of a dollar
entries.definitionCN: 价值百分之一美元的硬币

entries.definition: a period of ten years
a period of one thousand years
a long period of history

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the hundred to years, to soldiers and to the calendar.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把「一百」与年份、士兵和日历联系起来。

normal.en: Cent means a hundred, so a century is a hundred years packed together.
normal.cn: cent 意为一百，因此 century 就是一百年叠在一起。

normal.en: The Romans counted soldiers in hundreds, and the same word later counted years.
normal.cn: 罗马人按百数士兵，同一个词后来改为数年份。

normal.en: Decade is ten years, a century is a hundred, and a millennium is a thousand.
normal.cn: decade 是十年，century 是一百年，millennium 是一千年。

normal.en: The phrase turn of the century marks the line between two hundreds of years.
normal.cn: turn of the century 标出两个百年之间的界线。

normal.en: In cricket a century is a hundred runs, the same number in a game.
normal.cn: 板球里的 century 是一百分，同一个数字换个场景。

abstract.en: Picture a long shelf with one hundred yearly calendars in a row.
abstract.cn: 想象一整排架子上摆着一百本年度日历。

abstract.en: Picture a stone tower that has watched a hundred winters pass.
abstract.cn: 想象一座看过一百个冬天过去的石塔。

abstract.en: Picture a clock hand going round and round for a very long time.
abstract.cn: 想象钟表的指针绕了一圈又一圈，很久很久。

examples.en: This church was built in the twelfth century.
examples.cn: 这座教堂建于十二世纪。

examples.en: For centuries people crossed the river by boat.
examples.cn: 几个世纪以来人们都靠船过河。

examples.en: The batter reached his century with one clean hit.
examples.cn: 击球手一记干净利落的击球拿到了一百分。

dict_mnemonic.text: cent 是一百：把一百年捆成一束，就是 century 世纪。

root: 源自拉丁语 centuria（百人队），出自 centum（一百），经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A hundred years is the everyday sense, while a hundred runs in cricket keeps the same count in sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 一百年是日常义项，板球中的一百分则在运动里保留同一个计数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hundred units gathered into a single block.
core.cn: 核心意象：一百个单位被捆成一大块。

branches.en: The time sense counts years in blocks of a hundred.
branches.cn: 时间义把年份按一百一组来数。

branches.en: The sporting sense counts points or runs in the same block.
branches.cn: 运动义按同样的一百来数分。

branches.en: Both keep the Latin count of one hundred.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留拉丁语「一百」的计数。

branches.en: Historical phrases such as turn of the century depend on the time sense.
branches.cn: 世纪之交一类历史短语依赖时间义。

branches.en: The plural centuries often means a very long stretch of time.
branches.cn: 复数 centuries 常指一段很长的时间。

intro.en: Century belongs to a large cent- family built on the Latin word for one hundred.
intro.cn: century 属于建立在拉丁语「一百」之上的庞大 cent- 词族。

latinIntro.en: Centum, one hundred, and centuria, a company of a hundred, are the two Latin sources.
latinIntro.cn: centum（一百）与 centuria（百人队）是两个拉丁语来源。

items.meaning: a period of one hundred years
items.exampleCN: 这发生在一个世纪以前。

items.example: The walls have lasted for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这些墙已经存续了几个世纪。

items.meaning: the leader of a hundred soldiers
items.exampleCN: 一名百人队长守着城门。
百年纪念音乐会座无虚席。
这位百岁老人仍每天散步。
他们办了一场百年晚宴。

items.meaning: a company of a hundred soldiers

latinEntries.meaning: a company of a hundred men

definition_en: a formal set of actions on an important occasion, or formal polite behaviour
core_image: 一群人按固定次序完成一整套动作
scene: 婚礼上宾客按顺序站好，等待交换誓言。The wedding ceremony lasted an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 ceremony 指「典礼」（第 1 个义项：重要场合的正式仪式）；句意是婚礼仪式持续了一个小时。

senses.title: A formal event
senses.definition: a formal set of actions performed on an important public or religious occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在重要公共或宗教场合进行的一整套正式动作
senses.example: The graduation ceremony begins at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业典礼九点开始。
senses.why: The Latin source named a sacred rite, and the word still keeps that sense of a fixed set of actions.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指宗教仪式，这个词仍保留整套固定动作的含义。

senses.title: Formal polite behaviour
senses.definition: the formal behaviour expected on polite occasions, sometimes seen as unnecessary
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌场合所要求的正式举止，有时被视为多余
senses.example: They greeted us without ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他们不拘礼节地跟我们打了招呼。
senses.why: Once a rite sets the proper forms of address, following those forms becomes a kind of ceremony in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 仪式一旦规定了得体的称呼方式，遵守这些形式在日常生活中也就成了一种客套。

intro.en: Ceremony comes from the Latin word for a sacred rite, and English first used it for religious observance.
intro.cn: ceremony 源自拉丁语中表示宗教仪式的词，英语最初用它指宗教礼拜。

items.en: Caerimonia named a religious rite and the awe that went with it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caerimonia 指宗教仪式以及伴随的敬畏。

items.en: The adjective caeremonialis described what belonged to such rites.
items.cn: 形容词 caeremonialis 描述与这类仪式相关的事物。

items.en: Old French ceremonie carried the word into court and church usage.
items.cn: 古法语 ceremonie 把该词带入宫廷与教会用语。

items.en: English ceremony first means a religious observance or a formal rite.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语 ceremony 先指宗教礼拜或正式仪式。

items.en: The word widens to weddings, openings and the polite forms called ceremony.
items.cn: 词义扩展到婚礼、开幕式以及被称为客套的礼节。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the ceremony family, while the meaning group lists rites and formal occasions.
note.cn: 形近组沿 ceremony 词族展开，近义组列出仪式与正式场合的说法。

entries.definition: connected with formal ceremonies
very formal and correct in behaviour
in a very formal manner
a fixed religious act
a set of actions always done the same way
entries.definitionCN: 总按同样方式完成的一套动作

entries.definition: a formal religious gathering

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the fixed order of a rite to weddings, openings and polite distance.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把仪式的固定次序与婚礼、开幕式以及礼貌的距离联系起来。

normal.en: A ceremony is a set order of actions: everyone knows where to stand and what to say.
normal.cn: ceremony 是固定次序的动作：谁站哪里、说什么都有定规。

normal.en: Wedding ceremony and opening ceremony both mark a moment people want to remember.
normal.cn: wedding ceremony 与 opening ceremony 都标记人们想记住的时刻。

normal.en: Without ceremony means doing something plainly, with no polite fuss.
normal.cn: without ceremony 意为不带客套、直截了当地做事。

normal.en: To stand on ceremony is to insist on polite forms and distance.
normal.cn: stand on ceremony 就是坚持礼数与距离。

normal.en: Ceremonial is the adjective for the event, ceremonious for a stiff person.
normal.cn: ceremonial 形容仪式本身，ceremonious 形容拘谨的人。

abstract.en: Picture a line of people moving in step through a hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人踩着同一节拍穿过大厅。

abstract.en: Picture a stage with ribbons, speeches and a fixed order of turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一个有彩带、致辞和固定顺序的舞台。

abstract.en: Picture two people bowing slightly instead of shaking hands.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人微微鞠躬而不是握手。

examples.en: The award ceremony was held in the main hall.
examples.cn: 颁奖典礼在大厅举行。

examples.en: She left the room without ceremony.
examples.cn: 她不拘礼节地离开了房间。

examples.en: The old ceremony is performed every spring.
examples.cn: 这项古老的仪式每年春天举行。

dict_mnemonic.text: cere 联想到「因此」：因为重要，所以要按固定次序走完一整套动作，这就是仪式。

root: 源自拉丁语 caerimonia（宗教仪式、敬畏），经古法语 ceremonie 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The sacred rite gives the event sense, and the required forms of behaviour give the politeness sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 宗教仪式给出活动义，被要求的行为形式则给出礼节义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fixed sequence of actions performed in public.
core.cn: 核心意象：在众人面前按固定次序完成的一套动作。

branches.en: The event sense keeps the full public performance.
branches.cn: 活动义保留完整的公开仪式。

branches.en: The politeness sense shrinks the rite into manners.
branches.cn: 礼节义把仪式缩减为举止。

branches.en: Both rest on actions that follow a set order.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在按固定次序进行的动作上。

branches.en: Weddings, openings and graduations supply the modern occasions.
branches.cn: 婚礼、开幕式与毕业典礼提供现代场合。

branches.en: Phrases such as without ceremony reject the polite forms.
branches.cn: without ceremony 一类短语否定这些礼貌形式。

intro.en: Ceremony extends into ceremonial and ceremonious, two adjectives with different shades.
intro.cn: ceremony 扩展出 ceremonial 与 ceremonious 两个含义有别的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Caerimonia and caeremonialis are the Latin noun and adjective behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: caerimonia 与 caeremonialis 是英语词族背后的拉丁语名词与形容词。

items.exampleCN: 她那郑重的鞠躬显得冷淡。

items.example: A judge officiated at the wedding.

latinEntries.exampleCN: caerimonia 以 ceremonie 进入法语。

definition_zh: 确定的；肯定的；某个；某些
definition_en: sure about something, or referring to a particular person or thing without naming it
core_image: 一件事被钉子钉牢，不会摇晃
scene: 他反复检查门锁，才放心离开。I am certain the door is locked.
sceneCN: 这里 certain 指「确定的」（第 1 个义项：对某事有把握）；句意是我确定门已经锁好了。

senses.title: Sure and without doubt
senses.definition: having no doubt that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 毫不怀疑某事为真或将会发生
senses.example: She is certain that she locked the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她确定自己锁了门。
senses.why: The Latin root certus meant settled and decided, so the word names a matter that no longer wavers.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 certus 意为已定下、已决断，因此这个词指不再摇摆的事。

senses.title: A particular one
senses.definition: used to point to a particular person or thing without naming it
senses.definitionCN: 用于指向某个特定的人或物而不点明
senses.example: A certain man called while you were out.
senses.exampleCN: 你出去时有个男人打来电话。
senses.why: If a thing is settled and identifiable, one can point to it while keeping its name back, which produces this use.
senses.whyCN: 既然一件事已定且可辨认，就能一边指向它一边不点名，于是产生了这种用法。

intro.en: Certain comes from a Latin adjective meaning settled, and it still describes what is fixed and sure.
intro.cn: certain 源自一个意为「已定下」的拉丁语形容词，至今仍描述固定可靠之事。

items.en: Certus meant decided, settled and free from doubt.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certus 意为已决断、已定下、无可怀疑。

items.en: The verb cernere, to sift or decide, stands behind that adjective.
items.cn: 动词 cernere（筛分、判定）是该形容词的来源。

items.en: Old French certain softened the ending and carried the word north.
items.cn: 古法语 certain 改变了词尾，把该词带向北方。

items.en: English certain first means sure and firmly settled.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 certain 先表示确定的、稳固的。

items.en: The word also marks an unnamed particular, as in a certain person.
items.cn: 这个词还标记未点明的特定对象，如 a certain person。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the cert- family, while the meaning group lists words for sureness and for a particular one.
note.cn: 形近组沿 cert- 词族展开，近义组列出表示确信与特定对象的词。

entries.definition: without any doubt
the state of being sure
not sure or not decided
having confidence that something is true
clear and not likely to change
one specific person or thing

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cert- family, the phrases for sureness and the second sense of an unnamed one.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 cert- 词族、表示确信的搭配以及「未点明的某个」这一义项。

normal.en: Certain, certainly and certainty all share cert, the idea of something settled.
normal.cn: certain、certainly 与 certainty 都共享 cert，即「已定下」的意思。

normal.en: For certain means without doubt, as in I know it for certain.
normal.cn: for certain 意为毫无疑问，如 I know it for certain。

normal.en: Make certain is the checking phrase: make certain the door is locked.
normal.cn: make certain 是核查的说法：「make certain the door is locked」意为确认门已锁好。

normal.en: A certain amount and certain conditions point to some without saying which.
normal.cn: a certain amount 与 certain conditions 指「一些」而不说明是哪些。

normal.en: Uncertain adds un- and flips the whole word into doubt.
normal.cn: uncertain 加上 un-，整个词就翻成怀疑。

abstract.en: Picture a nail driven flush into wood, no longer moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚钉子被敲平进木头，不再晃动。

abstract.en: Picture a judge striking a table and closing the case.
abstract.cn: 想象法官敲一下桌子，把案子结掉。

abstract.en: Picture a name written as a blank line, known but not shown.
abstract.cn: 想象名字写成一条空白线，知道却不明说。

examples.en: I am certain that the train leaves at six.
examples.cn: 我确定火车六点开。

examples.en: Certain plants need very little water.
examples.cn: 某些植物需要的水很少。

examples.en: We cannot say for certain what caused the fire.
examples.cn: 我们无法确切说出起火的原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: cert 像「确认」的缩写：已经确认过的事，就是 certain。

root: 源自拉丁语 certus（已定的、确定的），出自动词 cernere（判定），经古法语 certain 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: A settled fact gives the sense of being sure, and pointing at one unnamed item gives the particular sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 已定的事实给出确信义，指向未点明的某一对象则给出特定义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a matter fixed in place and unable to shift.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件事被固定住，无法移动。

branches.en: The sureness sense rests on a fact already decided.
branches.cn: 确信义建立在一个已经定下的事实上。

branches.en: The particular sense points without naming.
branches.cn: 特定义只指向而不点明。

branches.en: Both keep the core idea of something fixed and identifiable.
branches.cn: 两者都保留「固定可辨」的核心意思。

branches.en: The phrase for certain strengthens the sureness sense.
branches.cn: for certain 强化确信义。

branches.en: A certain person stays deliberately vague about identity.
branches.cn: a certain person 有意模糊身份。

intro.en: Certain builds certainly, certainty and uncertain, and the cert- stem runs through the whole group.
intro.cn: certain 构成 certainly、certainty 与 uncertain，cert- 词干贯穿整组词。

latinIntro.en: Certus, settled, and cernere, to decide, are the Latin pair behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: certus（已定的）与 cernere（判定）是该词族背后的拉丁语一对词。

items.example: There is no certainty in war.
items.exampleCN: 战争中没有什么确定的事。

latinEntries.exampleCN: certitudo 是 certitude 的来源。

definition_en: without any doubt, or used to agree politely to a request
core_image: 一句话被钉死，没有半点摇晃的余地
scene: 他点头答应，语气里没有一丝犹豫。She will certainly help us.
sceneCN: 这里 certainly 指「肯定地」（第 1 个义项：毫无疑问地）；句意是她肯定会帮我们。

senses.title: Without any doubt
senses.definition: in a way that leaves no doubt about what is said
senses.definitionCN: 以对所说不留疑问的方式
senses.example: The plan will certainly succeed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划肯定会成功。
senses.why: The adverb simply adds -ly to certain, so it carries the same settled sureness into the action.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是在 certain 后加 -ly，把同样的确定感带给动作。

senses.title: A polite yes
senses.definition: used in speech to agree strongly and politely to a request
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用于爽快而有礼地同意请求
senses.example: Certainly, please come in.
senses.exampleCN: 当然，请进。
senses.why: A speaker who is completely sure can answer with the adverb alone, and that firm answer hardened into a polite formula.
senses.whyCN: 完全有把握的人可以只用一个副词作答，这种干脆的回答便固化成了礼貌套语。

intro.en: Certainly is the adverb of certain, built on the Latin adjective for something settled.
intro.cn: certainly 是 certain 的副词，建立在表示「已定」的拉丁语形容词之上。

items.en: Certus meant decided and free from doubt.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certus 意为已决断、无可怀疑。

items.en: The adverb certa mente grew from the same stem in later Latin.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语中，副词 certa mente 由同一词干发展而来。

items.en: Old French certain supplied the adjective to English.
items.cn: 古法语 certain 把形容词提供给英语。

items.en: English adds -ly and forms certainly as a firm statement.
items.cn: 英语加上 -ly，构成表示坚定陈述的 certainly。

items.en: The word also becomes a polite yes in everyday conversation.
items.cn: 这个词在日常对话中也成了礼貌的「当然」。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the cert- family, while the meaning group lists adverbs of strong agreement.
note.cn: 形近组沿 cert- 词族展开，近义组列出表示强烈肯定的副词。

entries.definition: sure or particular
the state of being sure
not sure
certainly or undoubtedly
without question
in a way no one can doubt

normalIntro.en: These hooks pair the -ly ending with the cert- family and the polite yes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 -ly 词尾与 cert- 词族以及礼貌的「当然」配在一起。

normal.en: Certain plus -ly gives certainly: the adjective becomes the way an action is done.
normal.cn: certain 加 -ly 得 certainly：形容词变成动作进行的方式。

normal.en: Certainly not and most certainly sit at the two ends of agreement.
normal.cn: certainly not 与 most certainly 站在同意程度的两端。

normal.en: Almost certainly leaves a small crack of doubt, but certainly alone leaves none.
normal.cn: almost certainly 留一道小小的怀疑缝隙，单用 certainly 则一点不留。

normal.en: Answering Certainly at the door is the polite version of yes.
normal.cn: 在门口答一句 certainly，就是礼貌版的「好」。

normal.en: Uncertain plus -ly would be uncertainly, the opposite ending in doubt.
normal.cn: uncertain 加 -ly 是 uncertainly，方向相反，落在怀疑上。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp pressed down hard on a document.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章被重重按在文件上。

abstract.en: Picture a head nodding once, firmly, with no hesitation.
abstract.cn: 想象一次干脆的点头，毫无迟疑。

abstract.en: Picture a straight line drawn without a single wobble.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画得笔直、毫不抖动的线。

examples.en: She is certainly the best player here.
examples.cn: 她无疑是这里最好的选手。

examples.en: Certainly, I can send you the file today.
examples.cn: 当然，我今天就能把文件发给你。

examples.en: The weather will almost certainly improve tomorrow.
examples.cn: 明天天气几乎肯定会好转。

dict_mnemonic.text: certain 加 -ly 就是「以确定的方式」：说出口时，仿佛在句子上盖了个章。

root: 由 certain 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，certain 源自拉丁语 certus（已定的）。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb states sureness first, and spoken use turns that sureness into a polite yes.
sensesIntro.cn: 副词先表达确定，口语用法又把这份确定变成礼貌的应允。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a statement sealed so it cannot wobble.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话被牢牢封住，不会晃动。

branches.en: The first sense states firm sureness.
branches.cn: 第一个义项表达坚定的确定。

branches.en: The second sense uses that sureness as agreement.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这份确定用作应允。

branches.en: Both come from the same cert- stem of settled things.
branches.cn: 两者都来自表示「已定」的同一 cert- 词干。

branches.en: Almost certainly softens the claim without reversing it.
branches.cn: almost certainly 只减弱而不反转这个断言。

branches.en: Certainly at the door signals welcome and consent.
branches.cn: 在门口说 certainly，表示欢迎与同意。

intro.en: Certainly belongs to the cert- group, where -ly marks the adverb and -ty the noun.
intro.cn: certainly 属于 cert- 组，其中 -ly 标记副词，-ty 标记名词。

latinIntro.en: Certus and cernere, the settled and the deciding, underlie the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: certus（已定的）与 cernere（判定）支撑着整组词。

items.example: We need certainty before we move.
items.exampleCN: 行动前我们需要确定性。
cernere 是 certus 的来源。

definition_en: an official document that proves a fact, a qualification or an achievement
core_image: 一张盖了章、写满事实的纸
scene: 考试通过后，她拿到一张盖着红章的纸。The school gave her a certificate.
sceneCN: 这里 certificate 指「证书」（第 1 个义项：证明资格或成就的正式文件）；句意是学校发给她一张证书。

senses.title: A document of qualification
senses.definition: an official paper showing that a person has completed a course or gained a skill
senses.definitionCN: 表明某人完成课程或获得技能的正式文件
senses.example: She has a teaching certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一张教师资格证书。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to make certain, and a certificate is the paper that makes a fact certain to others.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「使确定」，而证书就是把某件事向他人确定下来的那张纸。

senses.title: Written proof of a fact
senses.definition: a document that records a fact such as a birth, a marriage or an ownership
senses.definitionCN: 记录出生、婚姻或所有权等事实的文件
senses.example: Bring your birth certificate to the office.
senses.exampleCN: 把出生证明带到办公室。
senses.why: Births and marriages are facts that must be proved to strangers, so the same paper that makes them certain records them.
senses.whyCN: 出生与婚姻都是必须向陌生人证明的事实，于是同一张使事实确定的纸也承担了记录功能。

intro.en: Certificate joins the Latin words for sure and to make, so it names a paper that makes a matter sure.
intro.cn: certificate 把拉丁语中「确定」与「做」两个词合在一起，指使事情确定下来的纸。

items.en: Certus meant settled, and facere meant to make or do.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certus 意为已定，facere 意为制作或做。

items.en: Certificare meant to make something certain in writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 certificare 意为以书面方式使某事确定。

items.en: Medieval French certificat named the written document itself.
items.cn: 中古法语 certificat 直接指这份书面文件。

items.en: English certificate first names an official written statement.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语 certificate 先指正式的书面陈述。

items.en: The word covers birth certificates, school certificates and certificates of origin.
items.cn: 这个词涵盖出生证明、学业证书与原产地证书。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the cert- family of official proof, while the meaning group lists other papers and awards.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示官方证明的 cert- 词族展开，近义组列出其他文件与奖项。

entries.definition: to state officially that something is true
the act of certifying
officially approved in writing
an official permission to do something
a paper given on completing a course
entries.definitionCN: 完成课程后获得的文书

entries.definition: a written or printed record

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into make plus certain and attach it to the papers people keep.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把词拆成「使」加「确定」，并把它挂到人们保存的那些纸上。

normal.en: Cert plus ficare: make certain. A certificate is a paper that makes a fact certain.
normal.cn: cert 加 ficare，意为使确定；certificate 就是让事实确定下来的纸。

normal.en: Birth certificate, marriage certificate and certificate of origin are three common papers.
normal.cn: 出生证明、结婚证书与原产地证书是三种常见文件。

normal.en: To issue a certificate is to hand over official proof.
normal.cn: issue a certificate 就是交出官方证明。

normal.en: Certify is the verb, certification the act, and certificate the paper.
normal.cn: certify 是动词，certification 是行为，certificate 是那张纸。

normal.en: A certificate course ends with a paper rather than a degree.
normal.cn: certificate course 以一张证书而非学位收尾。

abstract.en: Picture a red stamp landing on a clean sheet of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚红章落在一张干净的白纸上。

abstract.en: Picture a frame on a wall holding one precious sheet.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一个相框里只装着一张珍贵的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a desk drawer where every important paper is kept.
abstract.cn: 想象一个抽屉，专门存放每一张重要文件。

examples.en: You need a medical certificate to join the course.
examples.cn: 参加这门课程需要一份体检证明。

examples.en: The certificate was signed by the head teacher.
examples.cn: 这张证书由校长签署。

examples.en: Keep your certificates in a safe place.
examples.cn: 把证书放在安全的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: cert 是「确定」，fic 是「做」：把确定的事做在纸上，就是证书。

root: 源自拉丁语 certificare（使确定），由 certus（已定的）与 facere（做）复合，经中古法语 certificat 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One sense covers proof of skill, and the other covers proof of a recorded fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个义项覆盖技能证明，另一个义项覆盖被记录事实的证明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper that turns a claim into an official fact.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张把说法变成官方事实的纸。

branches.en: The qualification sense proves a completed course or skill.
branches.cn: 资格义证明完成的课程或技能。

branches.en: The fact sense records birth, marriage or ownership.
branches.cn: 事实义记录出生、婚姻或所有权。

branches.en: Both make a claim certain through official writing.
branches.cn: 两者都通过官方书写使某种说法确定。

branches.en: Certificate courses build towards this first sense.
branches.cn: 证书课程朝着第一个义项积累。

branches.en: Birth and marriage certificates are the plainest examples of the second.
branches.cn: 出生与结婚证书是第二个义项最直白的例子。

intro.en: Certificate shares its stem with certify and certification, and -ficare marks the making.
intro.cn: certificate 与 certify、certification 同干，-ficare 标记「使…」的动作。

latinIntro.en: Certus, sure, and facere, to make, combine in certificare.
latinIntro.cn: certus（确定的）与 facere（做）在 certificare 中结合。

items.example: Show your certificate at the gate.

definition_zh: 链条；一连串；连锁店；用链条拴住
definition_en: a line of connected metal rings, a series of connected things, or to fasten something with a chain
core_image: 一个环扣住下一个环，连成不断的一串
scene: 他用一条铁链把大门锁住。A chain held the gate shut.
sceneCN: 这里 chain 指「链条」（第 1 个义项：相连的金属环）；句意是一条铁链把大门锁住。

senses.title: Connected metal rings
senses.definition: a series of metal rings joined together and used for pulling or fastening
senses.definitionCN: 一串相连的金属环，用于拉动或固定
senses.example: The dog was tied with a strong chain.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗被一条结实的链子拴着。
senses.why: The Latin source named a fetter, so linked metal is the oldest and most concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指镣铐，因此相连的金属是最古老也最具体的义项。

senses.title: A connected series
senses.definition: a series of things or events in which each one leads to the next
senses.definitionCN: 一环引出一环的一系列事物或事件
senses.example: A chain of small mistakes ruined the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 一连串小错误毁掉了计划。
senses.why: Linked rings look exactly like linked events, so the physical chain becomes a metaphor for a series.
senses.whyCN: 相连的环与相连的事件看起来一样，于是实物的链成了系列的比喻。

senses.title: To fasten with a chain
senses.definition: to tie or lock something with a chain
senses.definitionCN: 用链条把某物系住或锁住
senses.example: They chained the bicycles to the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把自行车锁在栅栏上。
senses.why: Once the object has a name, using it becomes a verb, so to chain means to apply that metal.
senses.whyCN: 物件有了名称，使用它便成了动词，因此 to chain 意为用上那条金属链。

intro.en: Chain goes back to the Latin word for a fetter and reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: chain 可追溯到拉丁语中表示镣铐的词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Catena named a chain or fetter of linked metal.
items.cn: 拉丁语 catena 指相连金属制成的链子或镣铐。

items.en: The small catenella described one link of such a chain.
items.cn: 指小形式 catenella 描述这种链子的一环。

items.en: Old French chaine dropped the middle sound and named the object.
items.cn: 古法语 chaine 省略中间的音，用来指这件物品。

items.en: English chain first names the metal object used to bind.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 chain 先指用来捆缚的金属物件。

items.en: The word extends to chains of events, chain stores and the verb to chain.
items.cn: 词义扩展到事件链、连锁店以及动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the chain family, while the meaning group lists other words for a connected series.
note.cn: 形近组沿 chain 词族展开，近义组列出表示相连系列的其他词。

entries.definition: fastened with a chain
the act of linking things
entries.definitionCN: 把事物链接起来的行为

entries.definition: to set free from a chain
a number of similar things in order
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序排列的若干同类事物

entries.definition: things following one another
a line of connected items

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the linked rings into events, shops and the action of locking.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子沿着相连的环，走向事件、店铺以及上锁的动作。

normal.en: Picture one ring holding the next: that grip is the whole idea of a chain.
normal.cn: 想象一个环扣住下一个环，这种扣合就是 chain 的全部要点。

normal.en: A chain of events means each event hooks onto the next like a link.
normal.cn: a chain of events 意为每件事像一环那样钩住下一件。

normal.en: Chain store and chain reaction both spread from one starting point through links.
normal.cn: chain store 与 chain reaction 都通过环节从一个起点扩散。

normal.en: In chains means bound, whether by metal or by rules.
normal.cn: in chains 意为受束缚，无论靠金属还是靠规则。

normal.en: To chain a bike is simply to put the object into action as a verb.
normal.cn: to chain a bike 就是把这件物品当作动词来使用。

abstract.en: Picture a row of paper clips hooked one into another.
abstract.cn: 想象一排回形针一个钩住一个。

abstract.en: Picture dominoes falling in a long unbroken line.
abstract.cn: 想象多米诺骨牌排成长长一列接连倒下。

abstract.en: Picture a locked gate rattling in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇上了锁的门在风中作响。

examples.en: The bridge hung on two heavy chains.
examples.cn: 这座桥靠两条沉重的铁链悬着。

examples.en: One small delay started a chain of problems.
examples.cn: 一次小小的延误引发了一连串问题。

examples.en: Please chain the gate before you leave.
examples.cn: 离开前请把大门锁上链条。

dict_mnemonic.text: chain 像「缠」：一环缠住一环，便成了一条链。

root: 源自拉丁语 catena（链、镣铐），经古法语 chaine 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The metal object comes first, linked events borrow its shape, and the verb makes the object an action.
sensesIntro.cn: 金属物件义最先出现，相连事件借用它的形状，动词义又把物件变成动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ring gripping the next without a break.
core.cn: 核心意象：一环扣一环，中间没有断开。

branches.en: The first sense keeps the literal metal links.
branches.cn: 第一个义项保留字面上的金属环。

branches.en: The second sense moves the links into time and cause.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把环移到时间与因果之中。

branches.en: The verb applies the object to the act of fastening.
branches.cn: 动词义把物件用于拴缚的动作。

branches.en: Both depend on one part holding the next.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖一环扣住下一环。

branches.en: Chain store and chain reaction extend the series to business and science.
branches.cn: 连锁店与连锁反应把系列义扩展到商业与科学。

intro.en: Chain forms chained, chaining and unchain, and it combines freely with other nouns.
intro.cn: chain 构成 chained、chaining 与 unchain，并能与其他名词自由组合。

latinIntro.en: Catena and its small form catenella are the Latin nouns behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: catena 及其指小形式 catenella 是该词背后的拉丁语名词。

items.exampleCN: 大门上挂着沉重的铁链。

items.example: The boat was chained to a post.

items.exampleCN: 链接数据可以节省空间。

items.meaning: a chain worn round the neck

definition_zh: 椅子；主席职位；主持（会议）
definition_en: a seat with a back for one person, the position of leading a meeting, or to lead a meeting
core_image: 有靠背、只坐一个人的那把座位
scene: 会议开始前，她挑了靠窗的位置坐下。She took the chair by the window.
sceneCN: 这里 chair 指「椅子」（第 1 个义项：带靠背的单人坐具）；句意是她坐到了窗边那把椅子上。

senses.title: A seat with a back
senses.definition: a seat with a back, made for one person
senses.definitionCN: 带靠背、供一人坐的坐具
senses.example: Pull up a chair and sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 拉把椅子坐下吧。
senses.why: The Greek and Latin sources named a seat, so the piece of furniture is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语与拉丁语来源都指座位，因此这件家具是最古老的义项。

senses.title: The leading position
senses.definition: the position of the person who leads a meeting or an organization
senses.definitionCN: 领导会议或机构的那个人所处的位置
senses.example: She was elected to the chair of the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她被选为委员会主席。
senses.why: The leader sat in the one special seat, so the seat itself came to stand for the office.
senses.whyCN: 领导者坐在那个特别的座位上，于是座位本身就代指了这个职位。

senses.title: To lead a meeting
senses.definition: to act as the person in charge of a meeting or committee
senses.definitionCN: 担任会议或委员会的主持人
senses.example: He chaired the meeting with great skill.
senses.exampleCN: 他十分熟练地主持了会议。
senses.why: Whoever holds the chair runs the meeting, so the office easily turns into the verb that names the work.
senses.whyCN: 坐主席之位的人负责整场会议，于是这个职位自然转成表示该工作的动词。

intro.en: Chair descends from a Greek word for a seat and reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: chair 源于希腊语中表示座位的词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.en: Kathedra named a seat, especially a teacher seat.
items.cn: 希腊语 kathedra 指座位，尤指教师的座位。

items.en: Cathedra kept the sense of a formal seat of authority.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cathedra 保留权威座位的含义。

items.en: Old French chaire named a chair or a pulpit.
items.cn: 古法语 chaire 指椅子或讲坛。

items.en: English chair first names the piece of furniture.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 chair 先指这件家具。

items.en: The seat grows into the office of chairman and the verb to chair.
items.cn: 座位义发展为 chairman 的职位与动词 chair。
